text: Look at scenes/main.aescene: read the tree, then the Player node and its script. Tell me in two sentences how the player moves.

content.text: The Player is a kinematic Body2D driven by the platformer-mode `Motion2D` component. Each `FixedUpdate`, `PlayerController` passes the `Move` input axis to `Motion2D.Move` and calls `Jump`/`JumpReleased` on the `Jump` button, so the component handles acceleration (60), deceleration (50), max speed (7), a 2.6-unit jump with jump cut, coyote time, jump buffering, ledge climbing and moving platforms. The script also flips the sprite and the Slash hitbox toward the direction you're moving, makes the body's hitbox active only while falling so you can stomp enemies, and bounces you upward with `Bounce` [0, -9] when an enemy dies.

The docs search found only one match for moving platforms: the `Motion2D.MovingPlatforms` field page. It's a single line: "Carries the character with the body it stands on." The Player already has this turned on (`movingPlatforms = true`, `platformOnLeave = keep`).

I added `Root/Ledge` at [-13, 1] with a default SpriteRenderer, as one Undo step called "Add Ledge". It's in the open scene in the editor but not written to disk until you save the scene. The scene's up direction is [0, -1], so smaller Y is higher, and 1 puts it above the Player at 2.9.

The Ledge is only a picture for now: the player can't stand on it yet. Its SpriteRenderer also has no sprite assigned, so it may not show up. To make it solid, it needs a Body2D and a collider like the ground nodes have (Body2D plus EdgeCollider2D). To make it a moving platform, its body would also have to move.
